findings.title: Default LIVE adapter can never resolve DNS
requirements: Task8 save/call URL validation
Task11 real adapter implementation
kill-switch NONE/REQUIRED permitted profiles
findings.minimalTrigger: Call validateProviderUrl on the valid allowlisted HTTPS endpoint without dnsLookup. The optional call returns undefined, and registry does not supply dnsLookup.
findings.consequence: All registry-created LIVE adapters fail before transport, including valid ACTIVE credentials and NONE.
findings.suggestedVerification: Exercise real registry -> adapter -> isolated HTTP for NONE and ACTIVE REQUIRED; normal DNS must use lookup or an authenticated pinned transport.

findings.title: SSRF guard neither normalizes all private addresses nor pins the checked connection
requirements: Task8 DNS rebinding/private/redirect refusal
Task11 test transport is NODE_ENV test and exact-loopback bound
Environment hard caps cannot be bypassed
findings.minimalTrigger: Injected DNS returns ::ffff:7f00:1, ::ffff:a9fe:a9fe, fe90::1 or 100.64.0.1; all are accepted. validate returns a hostname URL which default fetch resolves independently. liveEgressAllowed=true overrides AI_MOCK=true; transport/dns/allowlist options have no test-only gate.
findings.consequence: Fixing R01 alone exposes rebinding/private peers and release transport overrides.
findings.suggestedVerification: Normalize byte-level IPv4/IPv6 CIDRs, pin resolved IP and check actual peer, verify every redirect; reject non-test arbitrary transports and noninventory loopback; test AI_MOCK=true override rejection.

findings.title: Response-byte and timeout state are lost, so invalid/post-byte failures retry and abort can stall
requirements: Task7 before-byte connect/429/5xx only, one retry, jitter/Retry-After and shared deadline
Task6 AbortSignal/timeout ordering
Group4 timeout/cancel/retry
findings.minimalTrigger: Return 200 with malformed body: result is retryable=true/receivedByte=false after consuming bytes. Empty 429 is receivedByte=true and Retry-After:3 becomes25ms. Pre-aborted call still invokes transport. Pending reader.read is not raced/cancelled on abort.
findings.consequence: Guard retries parser/oversize/after-byte errors, omits permitted empty429 retry, ignores actual Retry-After/jitter, labels deadline abort CANCELLED, and can hang after cancellation.
findings.suggestedVerification: Isolated HTTP partial SSE/JSON then close; malformed200, oversized body, empty429/503, 4xx, connect failure, timeout, preabort and blocked body; assert call count, exact attempt reservations, elapsed deadline, safe public retryability.

findings.title: Required streaming adapter and HTTP contract coverage are absent
requirements: Task5 deterministic fixture chunks/usage/duration
Task11 request serialization, stream parsing, headers/body/429/5xx/timeout/invalidJSON/size isolated transport
findings.minimalTrigger: Adapter forces stream:false and parses only choices[0].message.content. Mock chunkCount only appears as a number in a JSON output. Tests fabricate Response objects in memory, not isolated HTTP or bound record-replay.
findings.consequence: There is no implemented streaming/SSE path and no actual HTTP evidence for required headers, fragmented multibyte content, error/usage mapping or cancellation.
findings.suggestedVerification: Use same real adapter code against a fixed-loopback test transport with split UTF8/SSE frames, bounded chunks, [DONE], usage, malformed/truncated stream, authorization NONE/REQUIRED, and zero public network.

findings.title: Resolution can assemble a mixed tuple and adapter can select a different model version
requirements: Task3 one DB consistency snapshot with same definition/version/revision
Exact ModelDeployment(id,configVersion) on every attempt
findings.minimalTrigger: Switch activation after definition include but before resolveModelSnapshot re-reads it. The first read stays revision1/providerV1 while second returns modelV2/providerV2. Registry selects deployments by id take1, without deploymentConfigVersion.
findings.consequence: Evidence can name modelV2 with providerV1 while actual adapter used modelV1; concurrent activation does not produce only complete old/new tuples.
findings.suggestedVerification: Real PostgreSQL interleaving switches between two complete tuples; accept old or new only. Put two model versions under same provider config, assert actual request model matches resolved composite key.

findings.title: Activation SQL lacks composite compatibility and monotonic CAS constraints
requirements: Final models3/6/9 composite FK/trigger compatibility, CAS revision+1
Task3 trigger rejects one-sided or stale activation
findings.minimalTrigger: The deferred trigger checks only PromptActivation versus PromptModelActivation promptVersion/revision equality. Independent deployment/provider FKs allow mismatched provider association. Updating both revisions backwards or changing status without increment satisfies it; PlanningPolicyActivation has only revision>=0. Service accepts no expectedRevision.
findings.consequence: Application-role SQL and stale commands can create invalid or backward activations despite declared DB invariants.
findings.suggestedVerification: Under real app role reject mismatched deployment/provider, rollback paired revisions, same-revision pointer/status changes, stale expectedRevision, and stale policy CAS; valid simultaneous+1 must work.

findings.title: Registered Phase013 adapter cannot complete real rotation and has ambiguous candidate identities
requirements: Task10 real active references, new immutable config, all revisions atomic
Task10 actual two-reference success/failure/concurrency/revoke PostgreSQL rerun
findings.minimalTrigger: prepareCandidates creates only a new provider version. activate retains old ModelDeployment version whose providerConfigVersion must equal the old value, so activatePromptModelTuple rejects the new provider version. listActiveReferences includes DISABLED; candidates collapse different source configs by providerId and lookups omit providerId.
findings.consequence: Normal rotation fails; after fixing that, candidates can be misbound across providers or disabled activations enabled. Existing Phase013 two-reference tests still inject refs.adapter backed by phase013_fixture, not this class.
findings.suggestedVerification: Run real ProviderConfigVersion/ModelDeployment/PromptModelActivation two-reference rotation, one candidate failure, competition/revoke, differing source versions and same numeric versions on two providers; preserve disabled state and exact key/client target.

findings.title: Prompt variable and response contracts are not enforced in the initial candidate
requirements: Task3 validate contentHash/schema/variables and shared runtime schemas
Frozen docs/prompt-design input/output exact contracts
CONFIG_ERROR/zero-call for invalid configuration
findings.minimalTrigger: Initial parser accepts arbitrary nonempty scalar strings, including invalid locale/date/timezone/stage; rejects valid structured array/object variables; never checks stored variablesJson. Guard marks arbitrary JSON {arbitrary:accepted} parsedOk=true; resolver also rejects every valid PromptVersion>1.
findings.consequence: Incompatible inputs and outputs are treated as valid, while legitimate next immutable prompt versions cannot be consumed.
findings.suggestedVerification: Use frozen eight-key input/output fixtures and negatives for formats/structure/unknown keys/max bytes; validate stored variable/schema binding; enable compatible version2; structure only, without pulling Phase017 repair business forward.

findings.title: Guard does not enforce owner, consent, privacy projection or provider region policy
requirements: Task6 owner/policy then input privacy before egress
docs/privacy-and-user-data sensitiveRequirementProcessing false/null forbids sensitive raw text
AI may not decide permission/consent
findings.minimalTrigger: Guard input has no authorized owner/profile/consent context; a caller may supply any travelRecordId and arbitrary userMessage. Only authorization/bearer/cookie string patterns are checked.
findings.consequence: After LIVE admission is repaired, private/foreign-owned or unconsented sensitive text can reach transport and be attached to another record.
findings.suggestedVerification: Server-owned authorization context with negative owner, absent/withdrawn consent, forbidden region/locale/data projection; all fail before reservation/secret resolution/network. Synthetic tests must be explicitly scoped.

findings.title: Quota and cost estimates ignore frozen settings and do not upper-bound the actual request
requirements: Final reservation Decimal conservative frozen pricing/input/maxOutput/fees upper bound
Task4 model context window
Hard constraints environment max timeout/cost and database quota
findings.minimalTrigger: With provider quota=1,cost=0.000001,model context=1/maxOutput=1 and env cost=0.000001 the guard succeeds, reserves2191 tokens and sends maxOutput2048. Estimate bytes/4 is a heuristic, not a proved upper bound. Cost uses one unversioned price, no frozen paid tariff/fees, and settled totals sum estimated not actual.
findings.consequence: Configured hard caps/context limits are bypassed and actual billed costs can exceed supposedly conservative reservations.
findings.suggestedVerification: Vary DB/env caps/timeout/modelparams, high-token Unicode inputs, known input/output pricing and fees, unavailable upper bound, and usage above reservation; all must remain within proven Decimal caps.

findings.title: Durable reconciliation/release is missing and unknown reservations disappear at the day boundary
requirements: Group5 settle/release/reconcile idempotent, cross-day unknown liability remains reserved
expiresAt triggers reconciliation only, proved NOT_SENT releases
Without provider reconciliation settle upper bound once
findings.minimalTrigger: Reservations are summed only where bucketKey equals today. No release/reconcile endpoint/service/worker exists; unknown stays RECONCILING until a new day ignores it. persistSuccess requires one update and is not an idempotent settlement API. Provider/DB exceptions can leave submitted RESERVED with no attempt.
findings.consequence: Unknown billed requests allow fresh next-day capacity; no bounded terminal recovery or exactly-once settlement can be demonstrated.
findings.suggestedVerification: Accepted then response lost, pre-send failure, cancelled/timeout, repeated settlement, retry each own reservation, expiration unknown mutation, and cross-day reconciliation under real DB concurrency.

findings.title: Mock enablement bypasses ADMIN service and approves before testing
requirements: First enablement same ADMIN service, synthetic run admin, fixture validation before activation and Phase014 settings update
No direct kill/config bypass or fake success probe
findings.minimalTrigger: enableMockAi trusts arbitrary actorId and callback, then updates SystemConfig directly without authentication/audit/receipt. CLI picks any ACTIVE ADMIN and passes probe async true, activates/enables first, then runs fixed-trace guarded probes; failures leave the flag enabled.
findings.consequence: An unverified fixture/actor can turn AI on; failures/re-runs can leave a partially prepared enabled environment.
findings.suggestedVerification: Exercise CLI/service with USER or non-run admin, failed fixtures/quota/audit, repeat invocation, and real Phase014 settings command; prove no activation/kill change on failed preflight and exact audit/receipts.

findings.title: Emergency kill and revoked keys are not rechecked before each dispatch
requirements: Goal bind kill snapshot before external call
Emergency disable/revoke precedes cache/TTL and new calls
Task10 emergency revoke interrupts real adapter use
findings.minimalTrigger: isAiEnabled runs once before multiple asynchronous lookups and reservation; decrypted adapter is retained for both attempts. Disable AI or revoke secret while waiting/after first retryable failure and next dispatch still occurs.
findings.consequence: A committed emergency stop/revoke can be followed by new egress using previously decrypted credentials.
findings.suggestedVerification: Delay before markSubmitted/transport, commit kill/revoke concurrently, assert no later request or retry and correct NOT_SENT reservation release.

findings.title: Evidence input hash is detached from transmitted messages
requirements: Each attempt exact inputHash/version/trace/duration
User messages remain separate and validated variables delivered as bounded user data
findings.minimalTrigger: Two distinct userMessage values with identical variables produce the same inputHash; validated variables are never rendered into system/user data at all. Arbitrary supplied userMessage becomes the full user payload.
findings.consequence: Evidence cannot identify the actual input and prompt tasks omit their validated structured data.
findings.suggestedVerification: Assert request payload includes exact frozen validated variable projection and separate user text, both hash-bound; changing either content changes inputHash; raw contents absent from persisted records.

findings.title: The declared eight groups omit required business assertions and mutation witnesses
requirements: Eight full business scenario groups and real negative controls
Test policies: count/name/overall PASS does not prove required assertions
findings.minimalTrigger: Initial dedicated report contains15 passed tests but no real ProviderConfig key references, NONE/no-decrypt success, ACTIVE REQUIRED success, expiry/reconcile/cross-day budget, genuine deadline, concurrent tuple switching, or full hash/schema negatives. Import scan covers only src/server and literal fetch/SDK strings, not src/app/lib or direct adapter import. Activation mutant removes model resolver status guard but prompt resolver rejects first, leaving test green.
findings.consequence: Eight group tags cannot authorize Gate PASS; a removed safety check may not produce the required red fixed fixture.
findings.suggestedVerification: Map every card assertion to executed leaf checks; add meaningful isolated HTTP and real DB cases, test true guard bypass/direct provider imports including app/lib, mutate the actual checked activation/reservation-CAS path, restore and execute all eight groups.

findings.title: Initial bootstrap policy and prompt content have no required frozen source binding
requirements: Final model9 typed freshness/planning/quality policy and task1/2 source-reviewed bootstrap
Task2 reviewed templates from docs/prompt-design with hash
findings.minimalTrigger: Policy is ad hoc quickDefaults/24h12h/maxDaily12/score0.8; there is no typed source/unit/bounds contract. The only Phase002 numeric freshness source is explicitly fixture-only seconds; Phase093 lists fields without values. Prompt template only tells the model to follow Phase002, with no supplied actual rules. Resolver accepts any valid-hashed policy content, including {}.
findings.consequence: Bootstrapped immutable v1 cannot substantiate declared planning thresholds or reviewed prompt contracts.
findings.suggestedVerification: Add an explicit Phase015 synthetic safe bootstrap derived contract with producer/source/unit/min/max/default and runtime scope/schema checks; do not rewrite frozen Phase002 inputs or claim fixture values are approved production. Bind prompt templates to reviewed docs and compare exact bootstrap source/hash. This remediation scope was agreed with root; no numeric values approved in this review.
